comparison: Both evaluate HRE as a novel DNA-binding element (C7, C59-C62, C64-C69). OpenEval finds strong support from ChIP-Seq and biochemical assays. Peer reviewers broadly support the claims but express specific concerns about 'Fig. 3. the EMSA to reveal binding,' indicating uncertainty about the quality of EMSA data (C65, C66), resulting in UNCERTAIN vs SUPPORTED evaluation.

Both evaluate HRE functionality through reporter assays and biochemical validation (C8, C9, C70-C76). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the modest induction levels are consistent with regulatory elements, while peer reviewers note the study 'covers a robust number of experiments' without specific critique.

Both evaluate S-HsfA2 as a transcriptional repressor (C77-C80). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the genetic crossing experiments and consistency across systems, while peer reviewers state the data 'broadly support the claims' without specific concerns.

Both evaluate HSP17.6B as a key target linking S-HsfA2 to heat tolerance (C10-C12, C99-C116). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the convergence of molecular, genetic, and phenotypic data as compelling, while peer reviewers note 'solid methods, data, and analysis' without specific critique.

Both evaluate the protein-protein interaction mechanism between S-HsfA2 and canonical HSFs (C16, C17, C124-C130). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches and substantial functional effects, while peer reviewers note 'ample experiments to support the claim.'

Both evaluate transcriptome data identifying S-HsfA2 target genes (C51-C56). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes good data quality but cautions that transcriptome alone cannot distinguish direct from indirect targets, while peer reviewers note 'robust number of experiments' without specific concerns.

Both evaluate heat-induced nuclear accumulation of S-HsfA2 (C57-C58). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mechanism of accumulation is not determined, while peer reviewers state the data 'broadly support the claims' without questioning the localization findings.

Both evaluate S-HsfA2 as a heat-sensitive transcriptional repressor (C5, C6, C41, C43-C50). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers additional structural claims (C38, C39, C42) not included in peer evaluation. Both emphasize the consistency of genetic evidence from multiple approaches.

Both address dual regulation of HSP17.6B. OpenEval (C13-C15, C117-C123) covers the full mechanistic model including promoter elements and antagonistic regulation. Peer review (C117-C121) focuses on the HsfA2-HSP17.6B interaction aspect. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate the noncanonical HSR mechanism (C14, C15, C122, C123). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the dual regulatory mechanism and mechanistic model, while peer reviewers explicitly describe findings as 'valuable' regarding 'mechanism that acts as a brake to prevent hyperactivation.'

Both evaluate S-HsfA4c characterization (C81-C88). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader set including S-HsfB1 data (C89-C98, C131-C132), while peer review focuses on S-HsfA4c. Both note parallel characterization approaches support functional conservation.

Both evaluate S-HsfB family members. OpenEval (C81-C98, C131-C132) covers both S-HsfA4c and S-HsfB1/B2a comprehensively. Peer review (C89-C98) focuses on S-HsfB1 and S-HsfB2a characterization. Both find evidence SUPPORTED and note comprehensive experimental approaches.

Both evaluate main conclusions about dual regulatory mechanisms (C18, C123, C131, C132, C134). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval synthesizes mechanistic findings into coherent model, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the study 'adds insights to our understanding of heat tolerance and plant growth.'

Both address structural characterization of S-HsfA2 (C38, C39, C42). OpenEval includes these as part of comprehensive functional analysis (R1), while peer review evaluates structural data separately (R14). Both find evidence SUPPORTED as foundational to understanding function.

Both evaluate the noncanonical HSR mechanism and regulatory balance (C123). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes dual mechanism integration, while peer reviewers specifically affirm the 'brake to prevent hyperactivation' concept as valuable.

Both address structural relationship between HSE and HRE (C64). OpenEval evaluates this as inference based on sequence analysis (R17, SUPPORTED), while peer review includes it with broader HRE characterization (R2, UNCERTAIN due to EMSA concerns).

Both address claim C134 about S-HsfA2 knockdown effects. OpenEval notes this is redundant restatement in discussion (R19, SUPPORTED), while peer review includes it with main conclusions (R11, SUPPORTED). Both accept the underlying data.
